summary: SurfNet is a quantum network architecture that encodes messages as surface codes and transmits them via dual channels: an entanglement-based channel for critical Core qubits and a plain channel for Support qubits, enabling fault-tolerant transfer with improved fidelity. The scheme combines benefits of teleportation-based and direct-transmission networks, supported by a custom decoder exploiting different error rates across code partitions and an integer programming routing protocol.
motivation: Quantum networks face fundamental trade-offs between reliability and efficiency: teleportation-based schemes suffer from low entanglement generation rates and communication overhead, while direct transmission schemes require transmitting many physical qubits per logical qubit, increasing network traffic and errors.
method: Surface codes are partitioned into Core (critical for logical error rate) and Support (auxiliary) parts transmitted separately via two channels with distinct error mitigation: Core uses entanglement purification (fidelity $\rho = \rho_1 \rho_2 / (\rho_1 \rho_2 + (1-\rho_1)(1-\rho_2))$ after purification), Support uses direct photonic transmission with re-encoding at switches. A modified decoder based on Union-Find grows clusters at speeds proportional to $-r/\ln(1-\rho_i)$ and achieves worst-case complexity $O(n\alpha(n))$ versus $O(n^2)$ for MWPM.
result: SurfNet demonstrates significantly higher average communication fidelity across network scenarios compared to entanglement-based benchmarks (Purification N=1,2,9), with similar throughput and latency; the SurfNet Decoder achieves 7.25% Pauli error threshold versus 7.1% for Union-Find decoder on distance-9 to distance-15 surface codes with fixed 15% erasure rate.
